reasoning: On 25 October 2022 the Board of County Commissioners enacted Ordinance No. 2022-41, amending Sections 26-101 through 26-103 of the Broward County Code of Ordinances to raise the county living wage from $13.27 to $15.00 per hour for covered employees with health care benefits ($17.17 for security services officers) and to require paid time off. The decisive provision is the indexation clause: beginning on 1 January 2024 for the living wage amount, and thereafter on 1 January of each year, the living wage and the health care benefit amount are each adjusted annually by the lowest of the increase in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) for Miami-Fort Lauderdale-West Palm Beach, three percent, or the across-the-board increase the County gives unrepresented employees. The action agenda records the item as enacted on a 7-0 vote and names this member in the meeting's attendance block. That is chair 1 - raise the wage floor and tie it to the cost of living so it rises automatically each year without new legislation - and the automatic annual adjustment is precisely the limb that separates chair 1 from chair 2, which raises the floor but adjusts it only when lawmakers vote to.
